archetype.name: Pocket Passer (downfield volume)
archetype.definition: A non-running quarterback in a pass-first offense whose value comes almost entirely from throws 10+ yards downfield and over the middle, with a shaky short game and heavy pressure around him.

report.headline: A real downfield breakout, but good defenses and a leaky line are catching up
report.take:
Bryce Young's fourth season looks like a different quarterback on the surface. He is throwing for 285.3 yards a game, second in the league and 97.1 more than last year, and his yards per attempt jumped by 1.21 to 7.51. Some of that is volume. Carolina passes more than its situations call for at the second-highest rate in the league (passRateOverExp 6.3), so he gets 38 attempts a game. But the efficiency moved too. After three seasons hovering around zero EPA per play (0.006 and 0.01 the last two years after a -0.173 rookie year), he is at 0.102 per dropback, comfortably above the league's 0.04.

Where the gains come from matters. Throws of 10+ air yards have added 57.4 EPA on a 10.3 CPOE. Everything under 10 yards, including screens, has lost value: -4.9 in total, with the behind-the-line throws alone at -14.1. Throws to the middle carry the passing game: 0.724 EPA per play, 72% completions. Tetairoa McMillan (54 targets, 0.429 EPA per target) is the main reason the intermediate game works. He is not a creator with his legs (34 rushing yards, six scrambles), so this is a pocket profile that lives on the seams and the sideline shots.

The numbers hide a split by opponent. His big EPA games came against Chicago, Atlanta and Detroit. Detroit now ranks 31st on defense, and the Week 1 361-yard line came in a 59-37 loss. Against the two best defenses he faced, Cleveland (7th) and Tampa Bay (3rd), he posted -5.9 and -20.3 EPA. The Tampa game had five sacks, two picks and a lost fumble, and he was off the field for part of the blowout. Over the last three games his EPA per dropback is down to 0.036 and his CPOE to -5, with the sack rate up to 8.5%. Third downs are a problem all year: -0.201 EPA with 8 sacks on 53 plays.

The protection story is mixed. He is pressured on 29.2% of dropbacks, 36th of 38, yet turns only 17.1% of pressures into sacks, 5th best and better than his career norm. That says the sacks are mostly on the line rather than him holding the ball. It also means losing right tackle Taylor Moton to IR is a real hit, not a footnote. The breakout is real in kind, since a 7.5 YPA downfield passer is a different player than the 6.3 version. The current level, though, is probably the ceiling, and the recent slide is the more honest preview against competent defenses.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep accuracy
strengths.body: On throws of 10+ air yards he is completing well above expectation, and those attempts have produced almost all of his passing value. The intermediate band (0.616 EPA, 9.1 CPOE) is the sturdiest piece, because it rests on more attempts than the deep shots and on McMillan winning in the 10-19 range. Deep EPA on 28 attempts will cool, but the aggressiveness bump and lower bad-throw rate versus last year suggest a real skill change, not just luck.

strengths.title: Owning the middle of the field
strengths.body: Throws between the numbers are his best area by a wide margin: 72% completions, 0.724 EPA per play, no interceptions. It fits a pocket passer who reads the seams cleanly. It also means linebacker coverage quality shapes his games more than corner play.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks for his pressure
strengths.body: Despite being among the most-pressured passers, he converts pressure into sacks at the fifth-lowest rate, improved from about 21% last year. He gets the ball out or away under duress. That limits the damage of a weak line, even if it can't erase it.

concerns.title: Falls apart against good defenses
concerns.body: His two worst games came against the 7th- and 3rd-ranked defenses, and the last three weeks show EPA per dropback down to 0.036 and CPOE at -5. Some of the early surge came against defenses that now rank near the bottom. This is the main reason to doubt the season-long efficiency holds.

concerns.title: Protection, now without Moton
concerns.body: Being pressured on nearly three in ten dropbacks is a line problem more than a quarterback one, given how rarely he takes sacks under pressure. Moton, a 71%-snap tackle, is on IR, and guard Damien Lewis is questionable. Expect the sack rate to stay around the recent 8.5% rather than the season's 6.9%.

concerns.title: Dead short game and third downs
concerns.body: Screens and short throws lose value, and third downs (8.2 yards to go on average) are where the drives die, with 8 of his 17 sacks. This is partly scheme and partly line, but it shows he struggles on the quick, on-schedule throws. It is a long-running trait rather than a new slump.

trend.note: He opened with three straight positive-to-strong games against softer defenses and peaked at 20.5 EPA against Detroit. The Philadelphia win was thin underneath (4.0 EPA, -8.2 CPOE), and the Tampa Bay game was his worst of the year.

nextGame.headline: Short week at Green Bay against a defense that limits big plays
nextGame.body:
Green Bay is the type of defense that has given him trouble. It ranks 9th against the pass and allows the third-lowest explosive-pass rate, and his season is built on explosive downfield throws. Quarterbacks score 13 PPR a game against the Packers, 5th fewest, and top tight ends have been held 5.1 points under their averages, the best mark in the league, which hurts Darren Waller's usual role. The opening is at receiver: WR1s have run 2.8 points over their norms against them, 25th, so this is a McMillan-heavy script. Green Bay's run game ranks dead last, but Carolina's run defense ranks 30th, so the Packers may lean on it, and the Book's 47.5 total still expects points.

Availability cuts both ways. Zaire Franklin, Green Bay's 99%-snap linebacker, is out, which is the most direct help for a passer who lives over the middle. Devonte Wyatt is questionable at defensive tackle. On Carolina's side, Moton is on IR and Lewis is questionable on a four-day turnaround. Jalen Coker, his second-most targeted receiver, is questionable with a shoulder injury, which would narrow the reads further toward McMillan. Winds near 10 mph with gusts in the low 20s could clip a deep ball or two but shouldn't change the game.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots versus a big-play-stingy secondary
keyMatchups.body: His 10+ air-yard throws are where all his value lives, and Green Bay rarely gives up explosive passes. If those throws turn into incompletions, his week looks like the Cleveland game: plenty of attempts, little efficiency.

keyMatchups.title: McMillan against Green Bay's WR1 coverage
keyMatchups.body: WR1s have outscored their averages against Green Bay, and McMillan is far and away his most productive target. With Waller facing the league's toughest tight-end matchup and Coker banged up, expect the ball to funnel to McMillan.

keyMatchups.title: Middle of the field without Franklin
keyMatchups.body: His best area is between the numbers, and Green Bay loses its every-down linebacker. That is the most concrete way this matchup tilts his direction.

nextGame.watch: Whether the patched right side of the line holds up long enough for him to work the intermediate middle. If he is getting sacked on third downs again by the second quarter, it's a Tampa repeat.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is sustainable: Carolina's pass-heavy lean and a defense that can't stop the run keep him at high attempt counts, so yardage should stay well above league average. The efficiency is likely to regress. Deep EPA on a small sample, a 10+ CPOE downfield and early games against weak defenses all point down, and his career says a 6.3 YPA passer doesn't become a top-ten efficiency one overnight. Moton's absence pushes the sack rate up. I'd expect something between his last-five and season lines: roughly 245 to 280 passing yards a game, 1.4 to 1.9 touchdowns, and about three sacks a week, with real blowup risk against top defenses.

He has no rushing floor, so his fantasy and real value are tied to the passing game working downfield. Turnovers have been modest (1.8% INT rate), and that part is consistent with who he has been.
swingFactors: Coker's shoulder and target depth behind McMillan

confidence.note: Six games, with a clear career-high change and the efficiency gains on small deep-ball samples.
